title: Morobe Governor Saonu forum opposing Wafi-Golpu deep-sea tailings placement
location: Sir Ignatius Kilage Stadium; S004 does not specify the locality. S005 reports a Lae forum the previous week that may be the same gathering.
participants_original: S004 says various communities around the Wafi-Golpu impact area and coastal communities attended, opposed deep-sea tailings placement, and supported Saonu’s call for alternatives; no numerical count is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. S004 says “various communities” attended and S005 says “many people” in Morobe accept the project apart from deep-sea tailings; neither gives a numerical or clear countable estimate of forum attendees. Eligibility remains pending_threshold.

title.summary: S004 identifies the Morobe Governor’s Wafi-Golpu forum; S005 reports a Lae public forum on the same project the prior week and may refer to the same event.

start_date.summary: The 12 February article says the forum was held yesterday, Wednesday 10 February 2021.

start_precision.summary: The article gives the weekday and date, establishing day precision.

end_date.summary: Neither report establishes when the forum ended; no date is assigned.

location.summary: S004 names Sir Ignatius Kilage Stadium but not its locality in the article text. S005 describes a Lae forum held the prior week; the articles may concern the same forum, but their venue/date link is not explicit.

scope.summary: The reports describe a public forum at one stadium in Morobe/Lae; no multi-site event is established.

organizer.summary: S004 says Governor Ginson Saonu organized the forum.

demands.summary: The reports describe opposition to deep-sea tailings placement and a demand that the Prime Minister and National Executive Council reverse the environmental permit. The local May 2015 codebook’s broad political behavior/process category covers policy choices by leaders; current supplemental procedure remains unverified.

participants_original.summary: S004 reports attendance by various impact-area and coastal communities. S005 says “many people” in Morobe accept the project except for deep-sea tailings, but does not count forum attendees.

participants_min.summary: Neither source states a numerical lower bound for forum attendance.

participants_max.summary: Neither source states a numerical upper bound for forum attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative phrases “various communities” and “many people” do not establish at least 50 forum participants.

protester_violence.summary: Neither article reports whether forum participants used violence; code unknown.

state_response.summary: Neither article establishes the state’s event-specific response to this forum or ultimatum. All seven response dimensions remain unknown; an earlier unresponded-to proposal is not coded as ignore.

eligibility.summary: A dated public forum and a policy demand directed to national authorities are reported, but attendance of 50 or more is not established; retain as pending_threshold.

notes: S004 body confirms a 10 February public forum organized by Governor Saonu. It reports community opposition to deep-sea tailings placement and support for alternatives; Saonu gave the Prime Minister and National Executive Council a 14-day ultimatum to reverse the environmental permit and said he would seek an injunction if it expired. The local May 2015 codebook’s broad political behavior/process category covers policy choices by leaders, so that demand is coded accordingly pending review of the current supplemental procedure. S005 may cover the same forum but gives no exact day or venue, so it is not a second event or independent attendance count. No headcount is provided.
